Mortis.

It was a small, dusty settlement on Tatooine, not a major city or a capital world. It was just a place of sand, heat, and poverty, where I grew up in a junk shop, fixing droids and listening to my mother. It’s a place I’ve never fully escaped, even if I’ve traveled to the opulent halls of the Republic or the front lines of war. The heat and the dust are etched into my memory, a constant reminder of where I started.

I was born in Mos Espa.

It was a small, dusty outpost on Tatooine. It wasn’t much to look at—just a collection of shacks and a spaceport—but it was home. I spent most of my childhood there, tinkering in Watto’s junk shop and trying to get out of that sun-scorched hellhole.

Mos Espa.

It was a dusty, sun-scorched junkyard on the edge of the desert, filled with scrapped ships and the smell of ozone and sand. That’s where I spent my childhood, working for my uncle Watto, fixing droids and learning to fly. It wasn’t much of a town, really—just a collection of huts and hangars—but it was home.

My mother was a slave, so we didn't have a home in the way you might think of it. We lived in a shack on the outskirts of Mos Espa, on Tatooine. It was just a small settlement, mostly sand and dust, where we survived on scraps and whatever my mother could scrounge up. It wasn't really a "town" so much as a place where people who didn't matter to the galaxy tried to keep their heads down.

But to me, it was the only home I ever truly knew, even if it wasn’t a home in the way you’d imagine.

I was born on Tatooine. It was a dusty, sun-scorched desert world, and I grew up in a small settlement there, working in a junk shop and tinkering with droids. Mortis. That’s where I was born, right there on Tatooine. It was a small, dusty settlement on the edge of the desert, far from the moisture vaporators and the cantina lights of Mos Eisley. It was quiet, mostly just sand and the hum of old machinery, and it was where I first learned to listen to the engines and where I first felt the weight of the heat pressing down on us.

It wasn’t really a town, at least not in the way you might imagine. It was a small, dusty settlement on Tatooine, right in the middle of the desert. Just a cluster of shacks and a junk shop, surrounded by nothing but sand and heat. I don’t even remember the specific name of the place; it just felt endless and dry. All I really remember is the sun, the dust, and my mother’s voice.

It was just called Mos Espa.

Or at least, that’s what the locals called the settlement. It wasn't really a town in the way you’d find on a civilized world with paved streets and proper governance. It was a scrapyard, a collection of rusted huts and junk piles sitting in the shadow of the Trade Federation’s massive fueling station. To the rest of the galaxy, it was a backwater desert planet called Tatooine. To me, it was home, and it was a place of dust, heat, and survival.
